q: A _____ capacitor is the simplest capacitor consisting of two parallel metal plates.
e: A parallel-plate capacitor is the simplest capacitor consisting of two parallel metal plates. Put cylindrical or spherical in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The surface charge density (charge per unit surface area) on each plate is expressed as $\sigma =$ _____.
e: The surface charge density (charge per unit surface area) on each plate is expressed as sigma = Q/A. Put QA or A/Q in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: If the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor are very close together, the electric field between the plates is _____.
e: If the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor are very close together, the electric field between the plates is uniform. Put radial or non-uniform in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

q: The magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals _____.
e: The magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals Ed. Put E/d or d/E in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is directly proportional to the _____ of its plates.
e: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is directly proportional to the area of its plates. Put separation or thickness in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows.

q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the _____ of the plates.
e: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the separation of the plates. area and permittivity belong to other processes, not this separation case. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The permittivity $\varepsilon$ of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum $\varepsilon_0$ as $\varepsilon =$ _____.
e: The permittivity ε of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum ε0 as ε = Kε0. K/ε0 and ε0/K belong to other processes, not this Kε0 case. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: Here K is the _____ or the relative permittivity of the insulating material.
e: Here K is the dielectric constant or the relative permittivity of the insulating material. Put dielectric strength or electric field in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum.

q: The permittivity of vacuum $\varepsilon_0$ is _____.
e: The permittivity of vacuum ε0 is 1. 6 × 10^-19 C. 8. 85 × 10^-12 C^2 N^-1 m^-2 is not 1.

q: For a vacuum, the dielectric constant K is _____.
e: For a vacuum, the dielectric constant K is 1. 0 is not 1, and >1 is not 1 either. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

q: For other insulating materials, the dielectric constant K is _____.
e: For other insulating materials, the dielectric constant K is >1. Put <1 or 0 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of _____.
e: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of vacuum. Put air or water in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: The dielectric constant K can be defined as the ratio of the capacitance with an insulator to the capacitance with a _____.
e: The dielectric constant K can be defined as the ratio of the capacitance with an insulator to the capacitance with a vacuum. conductor is not vacuum, and metal is not vacuum either. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: When a charged capacitor is disconnected and a dielectric is inserted, the potential difference of the capacitor is found to _____.
e: When a charged capacitor is disconnected and a dielectric is inserted, the potential difference of the capacitor is found to decrease. Put increase or remain same in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

q: When a charged capacitor is disconnected and a dielectric is inserted, the capacitance of the capacitor _____.
e: When a charged capacitor is disconnected and a dielectric is inserted, the capacitance of the capacitor increases. Put decreases or remains same in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: A dielectric provides an increase in _____ operating voltage.
e: A dielectric provides an increase in minimum operating voltage. Put maximum or average in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

q: A dielectric provides mechanical support allowing plates to be close together without _____ contact.
e: A dielectric provides mechanical support allowing plates to be close together without electrical contact. thermal is not electrical, and physical is not electrical either. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

q: A dielectric may be able to withstand a larger _____ between the plates than air.
e: A dielectric may be able to withstand a larger electric field between the plates than air. current is not electric field, and resistance is not electric field either. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

e: According to Table 9. 1, the dielectric constant of Water (18°C) is 81. Put 28. 4 or 25 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics.

q: According to Table 9.1, the dielectric constant of Paper is _____.

q: According to Table 9.1, the dielectric constant of Mica is _____.

q: The permittivity of vacuum $\varepsilon_0$ can also be expressed in the unit _____.
e: The permittivity of vacuum ε0 can also be expressed in the unit A s^-1. F m^-1 is not A s^-1, and C V^-1 is not A s^-1 either. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum.

q: According to Table 9.1, the dielectric constant of Nylon (solid) is _____.

q: According to Table 9.1, the dielectric constant of Rubber (hard) is _____.

e: According to Table 9. 1, the dielectric constant of Waxed paper is 2. Put 1 or 3 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.
